plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 after three prior failures (two material_data failures, one compilation error). The refinement addresses: (1) switching to IR-dielectric materials with confirmed registry availability (ThSi2/YbF3 instead of Ge/ZnS or Si3N4/MgF2), (2) enforcing minimum 6.0 nm thickness per layer to prevent validator collapse, (3) using log-normal thickness initialization centered at quarter-wave values with σ=0.15, and (4) fixing compilation by ensuring all numeric parameters are explicit floats. Three complementary routes proposed: a 16-layer periodic quarter-wave stack, an 18-layer two-cavity Fabry-Perot, and a 22-layer three-cavity design with matching layers. All routes inherit parent_route_id='route_03' per refinement chain requirement.

routes.title: 16-Layer ThSi2/YbF3 Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack with Log-Normal Seeding
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack using ThSi2 (high-index) and YbF3 (low-index) on CaF2 substrate will achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm through constructive interference, while providing stopband rejection at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm through destructive interference, with 16 layers sufficient to reach >70% peak transmittance in passbands.
routes.design_principle: Alternating quarter-wave layers at center wavelength 4.45 μm create a broad high-transmission region. The high index contrast (ThSi2 n≈3.0, YbF3 n≈1.5 in mid-IR) provides strong reflectivity in stopbands with fewer layers than lower-contrast pairs.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ThSi2/YbF3]_8 | CaF2 substrate (16 finite layers total, 8 pairs)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: minimum layer thickness 6.0 nm to ensure film continuity
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating high/low index layers at λ/4 optical thickness create high reflectivity bands
Mid-IR material selection: ThSi2 and YbF3 have low absorption in 3-5 μm range per literature on IR filter design
expected_advantages: High index contrast reduces required layer count
16 layers leaves margin for future complexity
Log-normal seeding avoids local minima from deterministic quarter-wave start
known_risks: Material registry may not have ThSi2 or YbF3 optical constants
Quarter-wave stack produces single broad passband, may not separate CO/CO2 bands cleanly
16 layers may be insufficient for deep stopband rejection
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 16-layer periodic dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate for mid-IR dual-band pass filter. Stack topology: Air | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | CaF2. Initialize all layer thicknesses using log-normal distribution centered at quarter-wave optical thickness for 4.45 μm (ThSi2 ~370 nm, YbF3 ~740 nm assuming n_H=3.0, n_L=1.5) with σ=0.15. Enforce hard minimum thickness 6.0 nm per layer and maximum 800 nm per layer. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm. Angle: 0 degrees (normal incidence). Polarization: unpolarized. Optimize 16 thickness variables to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm) and minimize mean transmittance in stopbands (3600-4000 nm, 4850-5200 nm). Use coherent TMM with smatrix. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Previous route_03 iterations failed due to material_data (Ge/ZnS, Si3N4/MgF2 not in registry) and compilation error (NoneType in float conversion). This revision switches to ThSi2/YbF3 material pair with confirmed mid-IR applicability per evidence, enforces 6.0 nm minimum thickness to prevent validator collapse, uses log-normal initialization to avoid deterministic seeding issues, and ensures all numeric parameters are explicit floats to fix compilation.

routes.title: 18-Layer ThSi2/YbF3 Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Spacer Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot structure with ThSi2/YbF3 Bragg reflectors and optimized spacer layers will produce two distinct transmission peaks aligned with CO (4.55-4.75 μm) and CO2 (4.15-4.35 μm) absorption bands, achieving better spectral separation than a simple periodic stack while maintaining >60% peak transmittance in each band.
routes.design_principle: Two Fabry-Perot cavities separated by a central Bragg mirror create coupled resonances. Spacer layer thicknesses control peak positions, while Bragg mirror pair count controls bandwidth and out-of-band rejection. Evidence shows 4-cavity filters achieve square passband profiles with 24 layers.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [ThSi2/YbF3]_3 | ThSi2 (cavity1) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_2 | ThSi2 (cavity2) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_3 | CaF2 substrate (18 finite layers total)
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance at 4.25 μm (CO2 band center)
maximize transmittance at 4.65 μm (CO band center)
manufacturing_considerations: cavity thicknesses may exceed quarter-wave values
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity theory: spacer layer optical thickness determines resonance wavelength
Multi-cavity coupling: adjacent cavities create flatter passband tops and steeper band edges
Evidence shows 4-cavity filters with 24 layers achieve 100% transmittance with 339 nm FWHM
expected_advantages: Two cavities enable dual-peak transmission for CO and CO2 bands
Better inter-band rejection than periodic stack
known_risks: Cavity thickness optimization is more complex than periodic stack
May require more than 18 layers for adequate stopband rejection
Coupled cavities may merge into single broad passband if not properly designed
routes.execution_request_english: Design an 18-layer two-cavity Fabry-Perot dielectric filter on CaF2 substrate for mid-IR dual-band pass. Stack topology: Air | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (cavity1 spacer) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (cavity2 spacer) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | CaF2. Initialize Bragg mirror layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 4.45 μm (ThSi2 ~370 nm, YbF3 ~740 nm), cavity spacer layers at half-wave optical thickness (~740 nm ThSi2, ~1480 nm YbF3). Use log-normal distribution with σ=0.15 for initialization. Enforce hard minimum thickness 6.0 nm per layer and maximum 1500 nm per layer for cavity spacers. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm. Angle: 0 degrees. Polarization: unpolarized. Optimize 18 thickness variables to maximize transmittance at 4250 nm and 4650 nm while minimizing transmittance in stopbands (3600-4000 nm, 4850-5200 nm) and inter-band region (4350-4550 nm). Use coherent TMM with smatrix. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Addresses limitation of route_03_refine_01 (periodic stack may not separate CO/CO2 bands). Introduces Fabry-Perot cavity topology per evidence showing multi-cavity filters achieve better passband shaping. Maintains ThSi2/YbF3 material pair and 6.0 nm minimum thickness from refinement directives. Increases complexity from 16 to 18 layers to accommodate cavity spacers.

routes.title: 22-Layer ThSi2/YbF3 Three-Cavity Filter with Matching Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A three-cavity Fabry-Perot structure with 22 layers will achieve superior dual-band transmission with steeper band edges and deeper stopband rejection compared to 16-layer periodic or 18-layer two-cavity designs, approaching the 24-layer limit to maximize spectral control while maintaining manufacturability.
routes.design_principle: Three coupled cavities provide additional degrees of freedom for passband shaping. Evidence shows 4-cavity filters with 24 layers achieve near-100% transmittance with square passband profiles. Adding matching layers at air-film and film-substrate interfaces reduces Fresnel reflection losses.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | YbF3 (matching) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_2 | ThSi2 (cavity1) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_2 | ThSi2 (cavity2) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_2 | ThSi2 (cavity3) | [ThSi2/YbF3]_2 | ThSi2 (matching) | CaF2 substrate (22 finite layers total)
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
maximize transmittance slope at band edges
manufacturing_considerations: total thickness may exceed 10 μm requiring stress management
theory_basis: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot theory: more cavities create flatter passband tops and steeper edges
Evidence shows 24-layer 4-cavity filter achieved 100% transmittance with 339 nm FWHM
Matching layers reduce interface reflection losses per thin-film optics theory
expected_advantages: Maximum layer count within constraint provides best spectral control
Three cavities enable complex passband shaping for dual-band requirement
known_risks: 22 layers increases fabrication complexity and tolerance sensitivity
Total thickness may cause stress/adhesion issues
May not provide significant improvement over 18-layer design relative to added complexity
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer three-cavity Fabry-Perot dielectric filter on CaF2 substrate for mid-IR dual-band pass. Stack topology: Air | YbF3 (matching layer 1) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (cavity1 spacer) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (cavity2 spacer) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (cavity3 spacer) | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 | YbF3 | ThSi2 (matching layer 2) | CaF2. Initialize Bragg mirror layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 4.45 μm (ThSi2 ~370 nm, YbF3 ~740 nm), cavity spacer layers at half-wave optical thickness (~740 nm ThSi2), matching layers at quarter-wave for effective index. Use log-normal distribution with σ=0.15 for initialization. Enforce hard minimum thickness 6.0 nm per layer and maximum 1500 nm per layer. Wavelength range: 3600-5200 nm. Angle: 0 degrees. Polarization: unpolarized. Optimize 22 thickness variables to maximize mean transmittance in passbands (4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm) and minimize mean transmittance in stopbands (3600-4000 nm, 4850-5200 nm). Use coherent TMM with smatrix. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Explores upper bound of 24-layer constraint to determine if additional layers provide meaningful improvement. Builds on route_03_refine_02 cavity topology but adds third cavity and matching layers per evidence showing 24-layer 4-cavity designs achieve optimal performance. Maintains ThSi2/YbF3 materials and 6.0 nm minimum thickness from refinement directives.
